lessons.title: Place and agreement
lessons.rule: Learn complete patterns for where someone lives and for describing a home. Lithuanian city and adjective forms change with their role in the sentence.
examples: Kur gyveni? Aš gyvenu Vilniuje.
Where do you live? I live in Vilnius.
Vilniuje is the city form in this learned location pattern.
Mano butas mažas.
My flat is small.
Butas and mažas are singular masculine forms.
Mano namai maži.
My home is small.
Namai has a plural form, with the matching adjective maži.

tasks.prompt: Choose the city form for “Aš gyvenu …”.
tasks.why: Use the learned location form Vilniuje.

tasks.prompt: Complete “Mano butas …”.
tasks.why: The adjective agrees with singular masculine butas.

tasks.prompt: Complete “Mano namai …”.
tasks.why: The plural form namai takes maži here.

tasks.prompt: Which question asks where someone lives?
tasks.why: Kur asks where; gyveni means you live.

tasks.prompt: Use the example to write “I live in Vilnius”.
accept: Aš gyvenu Vilniuje.
tasks.why: Keep the learned first-person verb and city form.

tasks.prompt: Use the example to write “My home is small”.
accept: Mano namai maži.
tasks.why: Use the matching plural forms namai and maži.

lessons.title: Time, reasons and conditions
lessons.rule: Keep past events, future plans and conditions distinct. Use a reason to explain a changed plan.
examples: Vakar dirbau. Rytoj dirbsiu.
Yesterday I worked. Tomorrow I will work.
Dirbau describes the past here; dirbsiu describes the future.
Negaliu ateiti, nes turiu dirbti. Gal galime susitikti penktadienį?
I cannot come because I have to work. Perhaps we can meet on Friday?
Nes gives a reason; the second sentence proposes a replacement.
Jei lis, susitikime kavinėje.
If it rains, let us meet in a café.
Jei introduces a condition, not a report that rain has already happened.

tasks.prompt: Complete the future plan: “Rytoj …”.
tasks.why: Rytoj refers to tomorrow; dirbsiu is the learned future form.

tasks.prompt: Choose the connector giving the reason for not coming.
tasks.why: Nes introduces the reason.

tasks.prompt: What does “Jei lis” express?
tasks.why: The clause describes a condition.

tasks.prompt: Which sentence proposes a replacement?
tasks.why: The question suggests meeting on Friday.

tasks.prompt: Explain that you cannot come because you have to work.
accept: Negaliu ateiti, nes turiu dirbti.
tasks.why: Connect the problem and reason with nes.

tasks.prompt: Write the learned café plan if it rains.
accept: Jei lis, susitikime kavinėje.
tasks.why: Use the condition first, then the proposal.

lessons.title: Connect events and explanations
lessons.rule: A connected account distinguishes events, a contrast and an attributed explanation. Do not present every sentence as the same kind of claim.
examples: Iš pradžių nusipirkau bilietą. Tačiau autobusas vėlavo.
At first I bought a ticket. However, the bus was delayed.
The first sentence reports an action; tačiau introduces a complication.
Atvykau vėliau, bet spėjau į susitikimą.
I arrived later, but made it to the meeting.
Bet contrasts the late arrival with the successful outcome.
Darbuotoja paaiškino, kad galime važiuoti kitu autobusu. Manau, kad svarbu turėti kitą planą.
The employee explained that we could take another bus. I think it is important to have another plan.
The first clause attributes information; manau marks the speaker’s view.

tasks.prompt: Choose the learned past action.
tasks.why: Nusipirkau reports the completed purchase in the example.

tasks.prompt: Which connector introduces the complication after the ticket purchase?
tasks.why: Tačiau introduces the contrast with the plan.

tasks.prompt: Who explains the alternative bus in the example?
tasks.why: Darbuotoja paaiškino identifies the source.

tasks.prompt: Which phrase explicitly introduces the speaker’s view?
tasks.why: Manau means I think.

tasks.prompt: Write the example’s contrast between arriving late and making the meeting.
accept: Atvykau vėliau, bet spėjau į susitikimą.
tasks.why: The outcome is contrasted with the late arrival.

tasks.prompt: Attribute the alternative bus information to the employee.
accept: Darbuotoja paaiškino, kad galime važiuoti kitu autobusu.
tasks.why: The reporting clause identifies whose explanation this is.

lessons.title: Concede, qualify and recommend
lessons.rule: A concession can accept an objection without making it decisive. Conditional recommendation forms and limited claims let you express a position precisely.
examples: Nors šis prieštaravimas pagrįstas, jis nėra lemiamas.
Although this objection is reasonable, it is not decisive.
Nors introduces an acknowledged concession.
Todėl siūlyčiau lankstesnį modelį.
I would therefore suggest a more flexible model.
Siūlyčiau makes a conditional recommendation, rather than reporting a past suggestion.
Toks sprendimas tiktų ne visiems.
Such a solution would not suit everyone.
Ne visiems does not mean that it would suit nobody.

tasks.prompt: Introduce the acknowledged concession.
tasks.why: Nors means although in this pattern.

tasks.prompt: Which form expresses “I would suggest”?
tasks.why: Siūlyčiau is the conditional recommendation form.

tasks.prompt: What is warranted by “tiktų ne visiems”?
tasks.why: The scope is limited: not everyone.

tasks.prompt: Does acknowledging a reasonable objection necessarily abandon the recommendation?
options: Yes, every concession reverses the position
No, the example distinguishes reasonable from decisive
tasks.why: A concession can qualify a position without reversing it.

tasks.prompt: Use the learned form to recommend a more flexible model.
accept: Todėl siūlyčiau lankstesnį modelį.
tasks.why: Use siūlyčiau for the recommendation.

tasks.prompt: Acknowledge the objection without treating it as decisive.
accept: Nors šis prieštaravimas pagrįstas, jis nėra lemiamas.
tasks.why: Preserve both the acknowledgement and its limit.

lessons.title: Attribute and limit a conclusion
lessons.rule: Reporting a source, interpreting evidence and recommending action are different functions. Preserve the qualification when reformulating.
examples: Ataskaitoje teigiama, kad registracija tapo greitesnė.
The report states that registration became faster.
This attributes the claim to a report.
Tai savaime neįrodo, kad sistema tinka visiems.
This does not in itself prove that the system suits everyone.
Savaime limits what the observation establishes; it does not deny every possible benefit.
Sprendimą vertėtų peržiūrėti gavus papildomos informacijos.
The decision should be reconsidered when additional information is available.
The recommendation names a condition for reconsideration.

tasks.prompt: Which wording explicitly attributes a claim?
tasks.why: The reporting construction identifies the source.

tasks.prompt: What does “savaime neįrodo” limit?
options: What follows from that observation alone
tasks.why: It limits the inference rather than denying everything.

tasks.prompt: Which reformulation preserves the second example?
options: This observation alone does not establish suitability for all
tasks.why: Preserve the evidential limit.

tasks.prompt: What triggers reconsideration in the third example?
options: The absence of every possible question
tasks.why: Gavus papildomos informacijos names the condition.

tasks.prompt: State the learned limit on the general conclusion.
accept: Tai savaime neįrodo, kad sistema tinka visiems.
tasks.why: Do not drop savaime or the scope visiems.

tasks.prompt: Give the conditional reconsideration recommendation.
accept: Sprendimą vertėtų peržiūrėti gavus papildomos informacijos.
tasks.why: Preserve the condition for review.

lessons.title: Negation, entailment and revision conditions
lessons.rule: Fine differences in the scope of negation and conditional language can change an argument. Reformulate without strengthening what follows.
examples: Ne visi dalyviai sutiko. Nė vienas dalyvis nesutiko.
Not all participants agreed. Not a single participant agreed.
The first sentence does not entail the second.
Iš to neseka, kad bet koks pokytis būtų žalingas.
It does not follow that any change would be harmful.
Rejecting that inference does not establish that every change is safe.
Jeigu atsirastų naujų duomenų, reikėtų peržiūrėti rekomendaciją.
If new evidence emerged, the recommendation would need review.
The hypothetical condition supplies a genuine revision trigger.

tasks.prompt: Which conclusion follows from “Ne visi dalyviai sutiko”?
tasks.why: Do not widen not all into none.

tasks.prompt: Which sentence expresses the stronger negative claim?
options: Both necessarily mean the same thing.
tasks.why: Nė vienas excludes every participant.

tasks.prompt: Does rejecting an inference of harm prove universal safety?
options: Only if the sentence is short
tasks.why: Failure of one inference does not prove the opposite universal.

tasks.prompt: What does the final example commit the speaker to?
options: Revisiting it if the named condition occurs
tasks.why: The condition specifies when the recommendation must be reconsidered.

tasks.prompt: Reject the overbroad harmful-change inference using the example.
accept: Iš to neseka, kad bet koks pokytis būtų žalingas.
tasks.why: Keep the inferential and quantifier limits.

tasks.prompt: Write the example’s hypothetical revision condition.
accept: Jeigu atsirastų naujų duomenų, reikėtų peržiūrėti rekomendaciją.
tasks.why: Preserve both the condition and the required consequence.

lessons.title: Origin, location and agreement
lessons.rule: Learn origin and location as complete patterns. Use ser for the quality in these examples, estar for location, and match adjectives to their nouns.
examples: ¿Dónde vives? Vivo en México. Soy de México.
Where do you live? I live in Mexico. I am from Mexico.
Vivo en gives a place of residence; soy de gives origin.
La casa es pequeña. La cocina está aquí.
The house is small. The kitchen is here.
Es describes the quality here; está locates the kitchen.
Los cuartos son pequeños.
The rooms are small.
The plural noun takes plural son and pequeños.

tasks.prompt: Say that you are from Mexico.
tasks.why: The learned origin pattern is soy de.

tasks.prompt: Complete the location: “La cocina … aquí”.
tasks.why: Use está for location here.

tasks.prompt: Complete “Los cuartos son …”.
tasks.why: The adjective agrees with the plural masculine noun.

tasks.prompt: Which question asks where someone lives?
tasks.why: Dónde asks where; vives means you live.

tasks.prompt: Use the example to write “I live in Mexico”.
accept: Vivo en México.
tasks.why: Use vivo en for residence.

tasks.prompt: Use the example to locate the kitchen here.
accept: La cocina está aquí.
tasks.why: Use está for the location.

lessons.title: Time, reasons and conditions
lessons.rule: Distinguish completed past events from plans and conditional alternatives. Give a reason when changing an arrangement.
examples: Ayer trabajé. Mañana voy a trabajar.
Yesterday I worked. Tomorrow I am going to work.
Trabajé reports the past event; voy a trabajar gives the plan.
No puedo ir porque tengo que trabajar. ¿Podemos vernos el viernes?
I cannot go because I have to work. Can we meet on Friday?
Porque gives the reason; the question proposes another day.
Si llueve, nos vemos en una cafetería.
If it rains, we will meet in a café.
Si introduces a condition, not a statement that it is already raining.

tasks.prompt: Choose the plan for tomorrow.
tasks.why: Voy a trabajar expresses the planned future action.

tasks.prompt: Choose the connector giving the reason.
tasks.why: Porque introduces because.

tasks.prompt: What does “Si llueve” express?
tasks.why: The clause supplies a condition.

tasks.prompt: Which sentence proposes another day?
tasks.why: The question proposes Friday.

tasks.prompt: Explain that you cannot go because you have to work.
accept: No puedo ir porque tengo que trabajar.
tasks.why: Connect the problem and reason with porque.

tasks.prompt: Write the learned café plan if it rains.
accept: Si llueve, nos vemos en una cafetería.
tasks.why: Preserve the condition and the plan.

lessons.title: Narrate and attribute
lessons.rule: Use the taught past forms to distinguish an event from its background. Connect a complication and outcome, and identify the source of an explanation.
examples: Compré un boleto, pero el autobús llevaba retraso.
I bought a ticket, but the bus was running late.
Compré gives the event; llevaba describes the background situation here.
Llegué más tarde, pero pude asistir a la reunión.
I arrived later, but was able to attend the meeting.
Pero introduces the contrast with the successful outcome.
La empleada explicó que había otra ruta. Creo que conviene tener otro plan.
The employee explained that there was another route. I think it is useful to have another plan.
The reporting clause identifies the source; creo marks the speaker’s view.

tasks.prompt: Choose the completed purchase in the example.
tasks.why: Compré reports the completed past purchase.

tasks.prompt: Which form describes the ongoing delay in the example?
tasks.why: Llevaba supplies the background situation.

tasks.prompt: Who explains the other route?
tasks.why: La empleada explicó names the source.

tasks.prompt: Which wording explicitly introduces the speaker’s view?
tasks.why: Creo que means I think that.

tasks.prompt: Write the learned contrast between late arrival and attending the meeting.
accept: Llegué más tarde, pero pude asistir a la reunión.
tasks.why: Preserve the contrast and successful outcome.

tasks.prompt: Attribute the other route information to the employee.
accept: La empleada explicó que había otra ruta.
tasks.why: Keep the reporting clause and its source.

lessons.title: Concession and conditional recommendation
lessons.rule: Acknowledge an objection without making it decisive. Conditional recommendation forms and the scope of a negative claim matter.
examples: Aunque la objeción es razonable, no resulta decisiva.
Although the objection is reasonable, it is not decisive.
Aunque introduces the acknowledged concession.
Por eso propondría un modelo más flexible.
I would therefore propose a more flexible model.
Propondría makes a conditional recommendation, rather than reporting a past proposal.
La solución no funcionaría para todo el mundo.
The solution would not work for everyone.
Not everyone does not mean nobody.

tasks.prompt: Introduce the acknowledged concession.
tasks.why: Aunque introduces although here.

tasks.prompt: Choose “I would propose”.
tasks.why: Propondría is the conditional form.

tasks.prompt: What does the third example establish?
options: It would not work for everyone
tasks.why: Preserve the scope of the limited negative claim.

tasks.prompt: Does a reasonable objection necessarily defeat the recommendation?
options: Yes, every concession reverses the position
No, the example distinguishes reasonable from decisive
tasks.why: Acknowledgement need not be abandonment.

tasks.prompt: Use the example to recommend a more flexible model.
accept: Por eso propondría un modelo más flexible.
tasks.why: Use the conditional recommendation form.

tasks.prompt: Acknowledge the objection while retaining its limit.
accept: Aunque la objeción es razonable, no resulta decisiva.
tasks.why: Preserve both clauses.

lessons.title: Attribution and evidential limits
lessons.rule: Separate what a report states from what the evidence establishes and what you recommend. Do not drop the condition in a reformulation.
examples: El informe señala que el registro se volvió más rápido.
The report states that registration became faster.
The reporting phrase attributes the claim.
Esto no demuestra por sí solo que el sistema sirva para todos.
This does not in itself prove that the system suits everyone.
Por sí solo limits the inference without denying every benefit.
La decisión debería revisarse cuando se disponga de más información.
The decision should be reconsidered when more information becomes available.
The recommendation preserves a condition for reconsideration.

tasks.prompt: Which phrase explicitly attributes a claim?
tasks.why: The reporting construction identifies the source.

tasks.prompt: What does “por sí solo” limit?
options: What the observation establishes on its own
Whether a benefit is possible at all
tasks.why: It bounds the inference.

tasks.prompt: Which reformulation preserves the second example?
options: This observation alone does not prove suitability for all
tasks.why: Keep the evidential limit.

tasks.prompt: What condition is named for review?
options: The end of all possible discussion
tasks.why: Cuando se disponga de más información identifies the trigger.

tasks.prompt: State the taught limit on the general conclusion.
accept: Esto no demuestra por sí solo que el sistema sirva para todos.
tasks.why: Keep por sí solo and para todos.

tasks.prompt: Write the conditional reconsideration recommendation.
accept: La decisión debería revisarse cuando se disponga de más información.
tasks.why: Preserve the trigger for review.

lessons.title: Negation, entailment and revision conditions
lessons.rule: Small differences in negation scope and hypothetical conditions can substantially change an argument. Preserve what follows, and what does not.
examples: No todos los participantes estuvieron de acuerdo. Ningún participante estuvo de acuerdo.
Not all participants agreed. Not a single participant agreed.
The first does not entail the second.
De ahí no se sigue que cualquier cambio sea perjudicial.
It does not follow that any change would be harmful.
Rejecting this inference does not establish that every change is safe.
Si aparecieran nuevos datos, habría que revisar la recomendación.
If new evidence emerged, the recommendation would need review.
The hypothetical condition provides a genuine revision trigger.

tasks.prompt: What follows from “No todos los participantes estuvieron de acuerdo”?
tasks.why: Do not strengthen not all into none.

tasks.prompt: Which sentence makes the stronger negative claim?
options: No todos los participantes estuvieron de acuerdo.
Both necessarily mean the same thing.
tasks.why: Ningún excludes every participant.

tasks.prompt: Does rejecting the harmful-change inference establish universal safety?
options: Only if the sentence is short
tasks.why: Failure of an inference does not prove the opposite universal.

tasks.prompt: What commitment is made in the third example?
options: Reconsider it if the named condition occurs
tasks.why: The condition names a real trigger for revision.

tasks.prompt: Reject the overbroad harmful-change inference using the example.
accept: De ahí no se sigue que cualquier cambio sea perjudicial.
tasks.why: Keep the inferential limit and quantifier scope.

tasks.prompt: Write the taught hypothetical revision condition.
accept: Si aparecieran nuevos datos, habría que revisar la recomendación.
tasks.why: Preserve both condition and consequence.
